name: Divider
summary: A thin line that separates two groups of content.
description: A divider is a hairline between two sections of content or two groups of controls: between items of a list, between a header and a body, between the actions of a toolbar. It is horizontal by default and vertical inside a row. A divider says that a topic or a group changes; spacing alone often says it as well, so a divider is used when the separation must be seen.

anatomy.description: Root: the line itself (an hr on the web). Carries the orientation.

options.description: A full-width line between stacked content, with space above and below. The default.
A line between items on one row (a toolbar), stretched to the row's height, with space before and after.

states.description: The only state: a divider has no interaction.

notes: Horizontal: the line spans the width of its container, with margin-block above and below.
Vertical: the line stretches to the height of its row, or to its minimum height when the row does not stretch it, with margin-inline before and after.

name.text: A divider has no accessible name: it exposes the separator role (an hr on the web), which assistive technology announces as a separator or skips, depending on the settings.

guidelines.text: A divider that marks a change of topic or of group is a thematic break: expose it as a separator so the structure it shows is available to assistive technology too. A divider that is pure decoration (a line under a heading) may be hidden instead.

Render an hr: it represents a paragraph-level thematic break and has the implicit separator role, without ARIA. A vertical divider says so with aria-orientation="vertical", a property of the separator role.

The line is decoration from the point of view of contrast: nothing depends on seeing it, so it needs no 3:1 against the surface (2.02:1 in light mode, 1.45:1 in dark mode on the default surface). A separation that must be perceived is also conveyed by spacing or structure.
A divider is never a target and never receives focus.

references.title: ARIA in HTML: hr element (role separator)
HTML: the hr element (a paragraph-level thematic break)
MDN: the hr element (implicit separator role)

examples.name: Vertical
examples.description: Between the items of a row; the stage shows its minimum height.

decisions.text: The divider is a 0.6 px line (stroke-width.sm) in the fourth neutral base border color (global.border.base.neutral.4), in every mode.
decisions.rationale: The Figma library's level edge borders are made for the edges of surfaces; the base neutral border is visible on the default surface without competing with text.

decisions.text: A horizontal divider has 16 px of space above and below; a vertical one 16 px before and after, and is at least 24 px high when its row does not stretch it.
A divider is a thematic break exposed as a separator (an hr); a decorative line is not this component.

changelog.note: Initial draft (decisions hairline, orientation-spacing, separator-semantics). An hr, horizontal or vertical (aria-orientation); no interaction state. Line contrast measured only: 2.02 (light) and 1.45 (dark) on the default surface.
